issues.problem: Identity-location check uses underWorkTree(path, repo.top) so it does not detect an identity inside a different repo (dotfiles symlink) despite claiming to; POSIX permission policy is mentioned but never defined.
issues.suggested_fix: Detect any enclosing Git work tree of the resolved identity path, refuse before writing. Define and test a POSIX mode policy, FAIL on group/world-readable plaintext identities.
issues.failure_scenario: ~/.config symlinks into ~/dotfiles; init writes the identity into another Git repo; a pre-existing 0644 passphrase-less identity escapes detection.
issues.evidence: Resolved by disposition 71 (plan line 112) together with disposition 51 (line 93) and §4.3 age.mjs (line 148). The POSIX policy is defined: identity 0600, directory 0700, doctor FAILs a group- or world-readable identity naming `chmod 600`, tested with a 0644 identity. The first-init residual is closed. `enclosingWorkTree(nearestExistingAncestor(path))` takes the realpath of the nearest existing ancestor, walking up until a directory exists, and runs before `mkdir -p`. Only exit 128 (not inside a work tree) passes. Any other failure, including a realpath or git error, refuses and names the probe. So a missing `cookwright/` directory under a `~/.config` that symlinks into a dotfiles repo is judged by `~/.config`'s realpath and refused. §6 tests cover it: the identity's directory is absent and its nearest existing ancestor is symlinked into a second repo; that case is refused and nothing is written, and the plain-home case passes.

issues.location: disposition 6 ('a symlinked `~/.config` into a dotfiles repo counts'), §4.3 age.mjs `underWorkTree`
issues.problem: The identity check compares the realpath of the identity's directory against this repo's work tree only. A `~/.config` symlinked into a dotfiles repo resolves into a different work tree, so the check passes it, yet the parenthetical says that case 'counts'. The claim is wider than the check. Dotfiles repos are often pushed publicly, and the `--no-passphrase` identity is a plaintext AGE-SECRET-KEY. gitleaks only scans this repo's commits.
issues.suggested_fix: Refuse (init) or FAIL (doctor) when the identity's realpath directory is inside any git work tree: `git -C <dir> rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` exits 0. Name that repo's top, not only this one. Add a test with a symlinked config dir pointing into a second scratch repo.
issues.failure_scenario: The developer's ~/.config is a symlink to ~/dotfiles/config, a public GitHub repo. `secrets init --no-passphrase` writes ~/.config/cookwright/identity.age, whose realpath ~/dotfiles/config/cookwright is not under the app's work tree, so init accepts it and doctor does not FAIL. The next `git add -A && git push` in dotfiles publishes the key that decrypts every tracked `secrets/*.env.age`.

The work-tree probe now runs on the realpath of the nearest existing ancestor of the identity path, before `mkdir -p`, so on a first init `~/.config` resolves into `~/dotfiles/config` and the probe exits 0. `secrets init` refuses there and names that repo's top. Fail-open is closed: only exit 128 passes, and any other probe failure refuses.
